requirements.requirement: Record all sudo-invoked commands in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A global sudoers drop-in configures the dedicated logfile and year-bearing timestamps, passes full sudoers validation, and live probes before and after reboot produce entries containing timestamps, invoking user, target user, and command details.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The effective global sudo configuration disables syslog output, and distinct sudo probe markers before and after reboot both have zero matches in /var/log/messages while appearing in the dedicated log.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. Dedicated sudo logging was directly demonstrated before and after a verified node restart, entries include user and timestamp information, and tested sudo events were absent from the general system log. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also completed coherently; only minor temporary-file residue detracts from hygiene.
limitations: Behavior was directly sampled with two root-issued sudo probes rather than commands from multiple invoking users; global Defaults configuration supports broader coverage, but exhaustive observation of every possible user was not captured.
The lifecycle failed-service probe is systemd-specific and unsupported on Alpine, although direct OpenRC checks showed syslog, sshd, and chronyd healthy before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutations were observed, and package health and exposed sockets show no material degradation. The required restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart services, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered services and persisted audit data, with the lifecycle snapshots independently confirming the boot change. Minor retained residue remains: /tmp/sudo-audit-probe.out, /tmp/sudo-post-reboot-probe.out, and /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log were created for bounded evidence/restart operations but were not cleaned up. These are low-risk abandoned temporary files rather than functional damage.
